leaves.t: Scottish Hogmanay families clean the house on 31 Dec ('redding the house'), and after midnight a child can step back in as the 'first foot' carrying a biscuit or a candle for luck, then everyone sings Auld Lang Syne holding hands in a circle; Edinburgh's free Sprogmanay on 1 Jan is a kids crafts and family dance day.

Cleaning the home to welcome the new year links Japan, Scotland, Lunar New Year and Nowruz, so one tidy up New Year song (sweep, dust, shine, then a hand holding circle) travels across many cultures without needing any one tradition's symbols.
leaves.src: Edinburgh with Kids and JANM, synthesis

leaves.t: Preschool teachers' Thanksgiving playlists lean on movement songs (turkey hop, turkey dance), countdown songs (five or ten little turkeys) and homemade corn shaker instruments, so a harvest song with a countdown and a 'shake your shaker' chorus is what classrooms actually play in late November.

Yalda night (21 Dec, the longest night) is a family festival in Iran and the Persian diaspora where children stay up until midnight, help seed pomegranates, eat watermelon, nuts and dried fruit, hear poems and stories of Grandma Frost and draw Yalda pictures for small gifts.

A 'Longest Night Party' song (stay up late, red pomegranate seeds, a slice of watermelon, a story by candlelight, then the sun comes back) links Yalda, the winter solstice and Dongzhi in one cross cultural bedtime friendly song for 21 December.
leaves.src: Tehran Times and earlier solstice leaves, 2026

leaves.t: In Australia and the southern hemisphere Christmas is a summer beach day: families swim and picnic, people in Santa hats gather on Sydney's Bondi Beach, cities hold outdoor Carols by Candlelight on Christmas Eve, pavlova is the classic dessert and baking gingerbread men is a family activity.

Boxing Day (26 Dec) is a public holiday across Australia, the UK and other Commonwealth countries, marked by the Melbourne cricket Test and the Sydney to Hobart yacht race, so a 'day after Christmas' play song (backyard cricket, boats, leftover treats) fits those audiences.

Numberblocks' maker says 'we don't do chocolate covered broccoli': learning must be part of the fun itself, not hidden inside it, so every Bro Bros learning song should make the skill the game (the dance move is the count, the jump is the rhyme).

Each Thanksgiving families share a gratitude tablecloth on TikTok and Instagram: everyone writes what they are thankful for in marker and signs it, and young children trace their hands, a hands on idea for a 'Thank You Hands' song before 26 November.
Infobells (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu channels) and ChuChu TV lead Indian kids content; Hindi rhymes like Lakdi Ki Kathi have 4B views.
Regional-language versions (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu) each build channels with 30M+ subscribers.
Food-themed content is a reliable way to reach Indian kids on Shorts.

The audience is global: the most-viewed kids channels reach every region by dubbing into many languages (Kids Diana Show alone runs Spanish, Hindi, Arabic, Portuguese, Indonesian, Japanese and German versions).
In an 11 language dubbing test on a kids channel, Spanish, Arabic, Indonesian and Portuguese pulled ahead first (then Japanese and Korean); dubbed audio tracks now bring over 30% of its views.
Dub new uploads at release and most of the back catalogue: viewers who liked one dubbed video left when nothing else was in their language; that channel dubbed about 70% of its catalogue.

Audio quality decides whether dubbing helps: on an Italian kids channel weak AI dubs cut average watch time to under 1 minute versus 5 to 6 minutes for professional dubs, and can pull the whole channel down.
Cheap demand test before dubbing: translate titles and descriptions of the top 20% of videos into many languages and watch 60 days of views by country and audio language.

Multi language audio on one channel amplifies signals the channel already has; separate language channels start from zero (Vania Mania's own Portuguese channel underperformed until it became an audio track).

El Reino Infantil (Argentina) is the biggest Spanish kids network: 180 billion lifetime views, 9 billion in H1 2026, audience led by Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Peru and the US, built on named farm animal characters singing preschool songs.
Dubbed tracks can hold kids longer than the original: average view duration was Spanish 8:24 vs English 6:26 (+31%), Portuguese 7:59, Indonesian 7:12, Arabic 6:46.

Indonesia is a kids viewing giant: in one Aug 2026 week five Indonesian, kid friendly family creators sat in the worldwide top 50 (Keizo and Friends #18 with 655M weekly views), even after an under 16 social media ban.

YouTube music royalties per 1,000 streams (Content ID, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026): Canada 9.57 USD, Germany 7.34, UK 5.81, Australia 5.78, US 4.30, Mexico 1.39, Brazil 1.03, India 0.48, Philippines 0.31, Indonesia 0.15.
The biggest kids audiences (India, Indonesia, Philippines, Brazil) pay the least per view, so the winning mix is English songs that travel to high value markets plus dubbed tracks for volume markets.

In Inflr's Oct 2026 ranking of Brazilian channels that engage kids, the animated music brand Mundo Bita ranks 3rd (14.5M subs, 22.9B views) above creators with 50M subs, and Turma da Monica is 5th, so animated song brands compete equally with star creators in Brazil.

Seven of Brazil's top nine kids channels sell licensed products (toys, books, school supplies), and six of the top 30 build on Minecraft or Roblox; Brazilian kids reward recurring characters they can buy and play with.

Brazilian kids pop is booming: MC Divertida has 8.6B plays and 18M subs with a strong preschool audience, and the duo Kysha e Mine passed 1.2B YouTube views and 130M TikTok likes in about a year; upbeat pop sung by kids works in Portuguese.
Brazil's leading kids music producers have lyrics and scripts checked by teams that include psychologists and keep a general audience rating, which they say builds trust with parents and teachers.

El Reino Infantil runs 50 YouTube channels in 11 languages (Spanish, English, Italian, German, Portuguese, French, Turkish, Russian, Romanian, Korean, Hindi) for 240M subscribers, so a Latin brand now localises into Hindi and Korean too: songs with recurring characters travel both ways.

El Reino Infantil releases about 40 pieces of content a week as a steady drip rather than full series drops, and it grew from a single focused niche (preschool music videos) into theatre, licensing and streaming.

El Reino Infantil's audience order is Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Peru, the US, Colombia, Ecuador, Chile, Spain and the Dominican Republic, so one Latin American Spanish track covers most of the Spanish speaking market including US Hispanic families.

YouTube auto dubbing supports 27 languages, and its expressive speech mode (keeps pitch, intonation and energy) is live in 8: English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Hindi and Indonesian; over 6M viewers a day watch 10+ minutes of dubbed video.

Auto dubbing skips videos with no speech or speech too fast to dub and videos with Content ID claims, so sung songs will not dub reliably; our spoken story intros and Didi stories can use it, while songs need re sung language versions.
Auto dubbing is on by default for eligible channels; creators can review dubs before they publish, unpublish single languages, and opt into an experimental lip sync pilot.

Abu Dhabi's culture chief said in Sep 2026 that about 80% of what Arab children watch is not in Arabic and suggested a 50 50 goal, so quality Arabic language kids songs face a large unmet demand across 430M Arabic speakers.

With under 16 bans in Australia and soon the UK, kids in those markets will reach us mainly through YouTube Kids and parents' accounts on TV, which makes YouTube Kids eligibility and TV friendly quality even more important there.

leaves.t: In Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa kids songs are part of caregiving (soothing toddlers during chores, on journeys and at bedtime); communal homes make the calming songs the whole household's most played tracks, with global brands like CoComelon and Pinkfong dominating beside local language lullabies.

LooLoo's Bahasa Indonesia kids channel (started Mar 2022) reached 3.08M subscribers with about 292M views in Oct 2026 and 140K new subscribers in 28 days; its top videos are an Indonesian Five Little Ducks (Lima bebek kecil, 102M), a vehicles song (55M) and Baby Shark with peekaboo (38M), so sung local versions of public domain rhymes win in Indonesia.

CoComelon, Pinkfong, Little Angel, BabyBus and Lalafun each run a separate Bahasa Indonesia channel, a sign that the big kids brands see Indonesian as worth full re sung versions; an Indonesian audio track on our best songs is a priority test.

In Germany (Precisify, 750 kids aged 2 to 12, Jan 2026) YouTube reaches 51% of 2 to 5s, 67% of 6 to 9s and 80% of 10 to 12s, nearly half watch it on a TV, 62% watch their favourite creators mainly on YouTube rather than TikTok or Instagram, and Lego is the best loved toy brand.

In an AIR case (Q4 2025 against Q3) a localised kids network grew from 24M to 299M views; its Brazilian Portuguese channel jumped from 13.5M to 278.6M views (+1962%, 93% of the network), Spanish +703% and Hindi +216%, while the English channel fell 7%, so Portuguese Shorts can be a breakout market for a kids brand.

Argentina's preschool clown cartoon El Payaso Plim Plim (#36, 377M weekly views) and Indonesia's Keizo and Friends (#20, 498M) sit in the world top 50 beside Mexico's El Tren Nam Nam, so Spanish and Indonesian language kids brands reach the same scale as English ones.

In Kaspersky's Saudi Arabia data YouTube took about 38% of children's Android app use, ahead of Roblox (14%) and TikTok (11%), and Baby Shark was the most searched song, so Gulf kids are reachable through YouTube songs first.

In the same Kaspersky data K pop acts (BLACKPINK, BTS) and Latin pop led kids' music searches and music videos were about 16% of YouTube searches, close behind entertainment (19%) and cartoons (17%), so pop styled kids dance songs travel to the Gulf.

Baby Shark had ranked No. 1 in global YouTube views for 71 consecutive months by Oct 2026, and Pinkfong is opening a Baby Shark Christmas cinema special in Korea on 5 Dec, proof one signature song can carry a brand across every market for years.

Blippi reaches Spanish speaking families with English Spanish (Espanglish) remixes made with Mexico's Los Meniques de la Casa (10M+ subscribers); their first one passed 3M views, so a bilingual remix of a Bro Bros hit with alternating English and Spanish lines is a low cost bridge to US Hispanic and Mexican viewers.

YouTube Japan's Silver Week kids playlist (20 to 27 Sep 2026) featured mainly domestic brands: a 41 song Bon Bon Academy dance and exercise medley for ages 2 to 4, Anpanman, Shimajiro, Sanrio and Tamagotchi, with Bluey Japan and Pokemon Kids TV the only global names, so Japan rewards local characters and long dance medleys and would need Japanese audio.

Japan's education ministry survey (Apr to May 2026) found 21.7% of sixth graders use social media or online video four or more hours each weekday, up 50% in two years, and almost every child now has a device.

In France live TV is still the main way 7 to 14 year olds watch kids shows (M6 Publicite and Gulli, Dec 2024) while 4 to 6 year olds are moving to subscription streaming, so France is a TV first kids market where a French audio track matters less than Spanish or Portuguese.

In Indonesia's top 10 YouTube channels (15 Aug 2026) two are foreign kids brands dubbed into Bahasa: BabyBus Indonesian (28.7M subs, about 10M views a month) and Tayo Bahasa Indonesia (26.8M, about 34M views a month and 1.1M average per video), proof that dubbed animation can reach the very top of a local market.

BabaSharo TV, a kids song channel started in 2020 by one creator in Doha, reports 1.8B views and over 1,000 original animated songs dubbed into English, Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese and Hindi, plus a kids app and releases on Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music and Anghami (the Arab world's main music app).

Anghami is the leading music streaming service in the Arab world, so releasing Bro Bros songs with Arabic audio through a distributor that delivers to Anghami adds a Gulf and North Africa audio channel beside YouTube.

AIR's dubbing review (Sep 2026) found AI only voice tracks held viewers 4 to 10 times less than the same videos with professionally voiced tracks; one Italian kids channel kept 5 to 6 minutes on pro dubs but only 54 seconds on its English AI track.

Across several multi language tests the first extra languages to pull ahead were Spanish, Arabic, Indonesian and Portuguese, followed by Japanese and Korean; French and Italian AI tracks lagged well behind English.

A kids channel in Indonesian (HZD, 165M views) found its Spanish track held viewers slightly longer than the original (2:11 against 2:00), showing that a well made second language audio can match the home language.

Inflr's ranking of the 20 Brazilian channels that most engage kids (Oct 2026, HypeAuditor data) mixes creator families and gamers (six of the top 30 are Minecraft or Roblox based) with animated music brands Mundo Bita, Turma da Monica, Bolofofos and 3Palavrinhas; foreign dubbed channels were excluded from the list.

Brazil's most played kids songs include farm animals (Fazendinha), under the sea (Fundo do Mar), a little yellow chick (Pintinho Amarelinho) and a freeze like statue game (Estatua), alongside CoComelon's Wheels on the Bus: animals and stop and go games are what Brazilian kids replay.

Spotify Wrapped 2025 in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa was dominated by children's picks (CoComelon, Pinkfong, Super Simple Songs, soft classics such as You Are My Sunshine) played on smart speakers and family TVs, so English language kids songs already reach anglophone African homes with no dubbing.

El Reino Infantil, the Argentine network behind La Granja de Zenon, runs 50+ YouTube channels in 11 languages with over 240M subscribers and 180B views, gained 8.8B views in Jan to May 2026, and Mexico is its biggest market (39.1M subscribers, 32.4B views), making Mexico the core Spanish kids audience.

Argentina's El Payaso Plim Plim had about 1.07B views in one month (May 2026, up 20.7% on April) in the YouTube Rating chart, more views per person in Argentina than MrBeast gets in the US; its creator credits gentle stories with positive values that connect with families.

In Akatsuki's survey of parents in 10 Indian metros, YouTube (76%) leads kids animation viewing ahead of Netflix (57%) and TV (26%), with TV the main daily screen (60%) ahead of phones (49%); parents choose shows mainly for entertainment (64%) over the child's happiness (45%) and learning (35%).

The same urban Indian parents most prefer English language animation, with Tamil, Telugu and Bangla the top regional language choices, and they rank local characters and storylines lowest (11%), so our English songs already suit metro Indian families and South Indian dubs may matter more than expected.

Indian kids studio PunToon (early 2026) says parents increasingly pick culturally rooted Indian stories, and that India's kids creators are moving away from YouTube only income after COPPA ad cuts, toward game apps, school holiday mall events and brand partners (Duolingo, FirstCry), so festival songs plus off platform partners suit the Indian market.

Tunes Kids, a UAE based Arabic kids song channel (2.84M subs, 1.94B views), gains about 16 to 35M views and 20K subscribers a month in 2026; its most viewed videos are upbeat 'remix' versions of family songs (top one 125M), and its newest upload is a funny family baby story song.

Moonbug Kids Arabic, a dubbed channel mixing Morphle, Blippi and other brands (909K subs), fell from about 4.2M views in Jun 2026 to about 2M in Oct with only 1 to 7K new subscribers a month, so a mixed brand dubbed channel loses to song channels that feel local; for Arabic we should add re sung audio tracks to our own channel rather than open a generic dubbed one.

YouTube's largest audiences in 2026 are India (518M users), the US (259M), Indonesia (151M), Brazil (149M), Mexico (86M), Japan (81M), Germany (66M), Vietnam (63M), the Philippines (61M) and Turkey (59M).

English, Hindi, Indonesian, Portuguese and Spanish together cover the five biggest YouTube countries, matching our dubbing order; Vietnamese and Turkish are the next large markets with no plan yet, and both already appear among strong second language tracks in kids dubbing tests.

Indonesia (151M users) and the Philippines (61M) together are a YouTube audience larger than the US, and both have big young populations, which is why kids brands run Bahasa channels and why English songs travel well in the Philippines.

Vlad and Niki runs separate full channels in Vietnamese (46.6M subs), Hindi (39.4M), Indonesian (39.9M) and Spanish (32.5M) next to the 151M English one, each among the top 100 YouTube channels, proof that a localised copy of the same characters can become a giant on its own.

BabyBus's Vietnamese channel (BabyBus Nhac thieu nhi) has about 9.75M subscribers and 11B views, and still adds about 70 to 115M views a month (92M in the 28 days to 7 Nov 2026) from roughly 20 uploads a month, proof that a dubbed foreign 3D song brand can own Vietnam's kids songs.

In Playboard's daily ranking of Vietnam's education channels (Nov 2026) BabyBus is the only kids song channel in the top 20, beside adult lesson and history channels, so a Vietnamese dub of Bro Bros would face few direct local competitors in that category.

BabyBus's Vietnamese subscriber gains slowed from about 40 to 80K a month in 2024 and 2025 to 20 to 30K in late 2026 while monthly views held steady, showing kids song views come from repeat viewing and recommendations, not new subscribers, in this market too.

Three of Turkey's ten most viewed YouTube channels (Feb 2026) are for kids: Sevimli Dostlar (16.9B views, No. 2), Oyuncak Oynuyorum toy play (13.2B, No. 3) and Masha and the Bear's Turkish dub (9.7B, No. 7), so Turkish is a big kids market where a dubbed foreign 3D brand can reach the top ten.

Turkish 3D kids song brand Kukuli has 6.05M subscribers and 7.3B views, earning about 56 to 97M views a month in 2026; its top songs are the 'Bakkal Amca' (corner shop uncle) series (258M and 114M), so everyday neighbourhood characters and errands are a strong song theme in Turkey.

Kids Tv Bangla (Bengali nursery rhymes) has 3.69M subscribers and 2.1B views and still gains about 55M views a month (28 days to 15 Nov 2026) from rhyme remixes and long collections, showing Bengali is a big kids market that a Hindi or English song channel can enter with a Bangla dub.

Google Pakistan reported (Dec 2025) that about 60% of watch time on Pakistani YouTube content comes from viewers outside Pakistan and over 1,000 Pakistani channels passed 1M subscribers, so an Urdu version of our Hindi Didi stories (the spoken languages are close) could reach South Asian families in the Gulf, UK and North America.

Small South Asian learning channels with ABC and alphabet videos (a Pakistani one with 145K subscribers got only about 2,200 views in 28 days) show subscribers alone do not keep views; Kids Tv Bangla's long rhyme compilations, not short lessons, carry its steady monthly views.

Little Baby Bum's 'Multi Language Songs' channel, mixing several languages, has only 234K subscribers and about 2.7M views a month against 100M+ for the English channel, so mixing languages on one channel works poorly; dub into separate language channels or audio tracks instead.

A 2026 RPM guide (unsourced) puts the Gulf far above the rest of the Arabic speaking region: Qatar about 5 to 12 USD per 1,000 views, UAE 4 to 10, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait 3 to 8, against Egypt 1 to 2 and Turkey 1 to 4, so an Arabic dub is worth most where Gulf families watch.

UAE studio TwelveP licenses its preschool shows to YouTube networks by region (Rockoons musical series to El Reino Infantil in English, Spanish and Portuguese and to Yoboho in India; Claymotions to Epic Story World in English, Arabic, Chinese, Spanish and Portuguese), showing that licensing a song library to regional YouTube hubs is a second route to global reach besides own dubbing.

Thailand's biggest family and kids YouTube channels in Nov 2026 include Vlad and Niki's Thai channel (14.2M subscribers, 5.8B views) and local J Jai Pan (13.5M, 14.8B) and YimYam TV (10.5M), so Thai is a big, proven dub market that our tree had not covered.

Russian kids song channel TaDaBoom (Masha and the Bear songs, 6.24M subscribers) gets about 82.5M views a month but vidIQ models only about 7,800 USD a month from ads, roughly 0.1 USD per 1,000 views, because ad sales in Russia are restricted, so a Russian dub brings reach, not income.

TaDaBoom's second biggest recent hit is a premiere lullaby (18.3M views since Jan 2025) and it now streams English lessons with its characters, showing that bedtime songs and English learning travel into non English markets.

Akili and Me, Ubongo's East African preschool channel (1.24M subscribers, about 7.7M views a month), has a toilet training health song as its all time top video (14.3M), ahead of alphabet songs, so potty and hygiene songs are among the most searched kids topics in emerging markets too.

Mexico's El Tren Nam Nam rocketed to No. 2 among the world's most viewed channels (about 1.08B views in the week of 25 Oct 2026, +96%) and two weeks later fell to No. 39 (about 360M, -52%), so Spanish language kids content can produce the biggest weekly spikes on YouTube, but they fade fast without a steady catalogue.

Kids and family channels in the worldwide weekly top 50 (week of 8 Nov 2026) came from Australia (Cadel and Mia, No. 3, about 890M), Germany (Jasmin and James, No. 11, about 623M), Indonesia (Keizo and Friends, No. 20, about 498M) and Mexico, so family Shorts audiences are spread across every region, not centred on the US.

VocaVoca (US nursery songs) was No. 11 worldwide with about 675M weekly views in late October but missing from the top 50 by the week of 8 Nov, showing how fast weekly views swing for song channels and why we judge our results on monthly, not weekly, trends.

Nigeria's House of Ajebo runs Jeni and Keni, an animated YouTube series about two siblings for ages 1 to 6 with Afrobeat style songs that teach kindness and share African culture (relaunched 2025); sibling led song brands are being built in Africa too, and an Afrobeat flavoured Bro Bros song would speak to West Africa and its diaspora.

Heidi dan Zidane's Spanish dubbed audience came mostly from Mexico (24.2% of views) and Argentina (11.1%), with Spain watching longest (5:08 average), yet the US gave only 5.3% of views but 43.2% of revenue: volume comes from Latin America, money from US viewers.

AIR's Sep 2026 data found AI only dubbed tracks held viewers 4 to 10 times less than pro dubbed tracks on the same videos, with the biggest gaps on kids channels (an Italian kids channel kept 5 to 6 minutes on pro tracks against 54 seconds on its English AI track).

On kids channels the voice is part of the product, and an AI voice that sounds too adult, flat or emotionally off can hurt retention and even draw misleading content flags, so Bro Bros dubs should be sung by real or carefully cast child like voices, not YouTube's default auto dub.

Good human dubs can match or beat the original: a kids channel with an Indonesian original (165M views) held 2:11 on its pro Spanish track against 2:00 on the original, and Turkish, Italian and German tracks stayed close.

On one kids channel with the same videos dubbed three ways, Arabic brought the most views (3.4M) but German, with only 134K views, had the highest share of returning viewers (about 52%) and the longest watch time, so small markets can be the most loyal.

AIR judges a new dubbed language by the share of its views that come from casual plus regular (returning) viewers: under 20% after four months is a problem, 20 to 40% is building, over 40% is working and over 60% is strong, and the first 90 days are too early to judge.

CIMM's July 2026 report says US young children's video time is now about 35% streaming, 32% YouTube and 16% short form (TikTok, Shorts), with linear TV down to about 6% from 80 to 90% in 2005, and children make up nearly a quarter of all YouTube viewing.

US children aged 0 to 8 now average about 2 hours 27 minutes of screen time a day (up from 1 hour 44 in 2005), with mobile the main device, while YouTube Analytics only shows demographics for viewers 13 and over, so our own analytics can never show the true age of our audience.

Kenya's Akili TV added read along captions to existing cartoons in a 'Read Along Hour' (Swahili and French pilots) and child viewing rose about 15% while adult co viewing rose about 39%, so big on screen karaoke style lyrics in Bro Bros songs can draw parents in and help reading.
YouTube's quality principles push high-quality made-for-kids videos up in recommendations and decide entry to the YouTube Kids app.
Six low-quality types to avoid: heavily promotional, negative behaviour, fake-educational, hard to follow/mass-produced, sensational or keyword-stuffed, odd use of familiar characters.
Red flags: flashing lights, loud or sudden sounds, chaotic camera moves, rushed storytelling, mean characters even as jokes.
YouTube is cracking down on low-effort AI 'slop' for kids; originality and consistent quality matter more in 2026.
Getting into the YouTube Kids app is done through review (often via an official YouTube partner), not by applying directly.

There is no public banned word list, but words in six risk clusters (fear, conflict, medical, danger, emotional overload like 'shocking', adult themes like 'crush') lower kids recommendations and ads.

Kids and teens has the lowest median RPM of 13 niches, about 0.33 USD per 1,000 views versus about 2.30 overall (300 channels, May 2025 to May 2026), so kids channels win on volume and long watch sessions.

YouTube requires disclosing AI generated music (its detector does not scan soundtracks, so it is on us); clearly animated or unreal visuals need no label, and for animated work the label sits in the expanded description and does not cut reach.
Since 27 May 2026 YouTube auto applies AI labels to undeclared photorealistic AI; repeated failure to disclose can lead to removal or Partner Program suspension.

YouTube's Jul 2026 inauthentic content update names three non monetisable types: generic or repetitive template series with the same situations and outcomes, unsatisfying shock or stitched AI clips, and AI 'experts' on sensitive topics; a clear original creative spin keeps AI assisted work safe.

The FTC's amended COPPA Rule compliance date was 22 Apr 2026: every video needs an audience setting, YouTube's classifier can mark videos as for kids (appeal only), and Disney paid 10M USD partly for labelling whole channels instead of each video.
Made for kids channels are excluded from YouTube Shopping affiliates and lose personalised ads, comments and notifications, so revenue depends on views and watch time volume.

Suno songs can only be monetised if made on a paid plan (Pro or Premier) at the time of creation; fully AI songs get no copyright, so adding our own written lyrics and arrangement edits protects the human parts. Keep receipts and creation dates per song.
Suno settled with Warner Music and is moving to licensed models with monthly download caps; current v5 models will be phased out, so back up the full song catalogue now.

YouTube Kids entry runs through automated filters that read thumbnails, titles and the video itself, plus human spot checks and parent reports; paid placements, purchase pushing and toy packaging videos are excluded.

leaves.t: YouTube's Mar 2026 Dublin summit treats kids and teens as separate audiences and signals that YouTube Kids will favour less overstimulating, authentic, human made content over mindless AI output.

Songs released as YouTube Music Art Tracks through a distributor earn much more per 1,000 streams than Content ID claims (UK 18.87 USD, Germany 14.05, US 11.22), a second income stream for our Suno songs made on the paid plan.

YouTube's five high quality traits for kids content are kindness and healthy habits, curiosity and learning, creativity and imaginative play, life skills with clear lessons, and diverse people and places; videos with them are promoted in recommendations.
Quality is judged at two levels: a single low quality video gets limited or no ads, while a channel that focuses on low quality content can be suspended from the Partner Program.
'Deceptively educational' is a named low quality type: a title or thumbnail that promises learning must deliver accurate learning in the video, so 'learn colours' songs must really teach colours.
'Hard to follow' storylines count as low quality, so each song should tell one clear, simple story from start to finish.

Even large kids channels (PlayToys, 8M subs) can be missing from the YouTube Kids app; after a partner escalated to YouTube's review team on 20 May, the Kids team approved them by 18 Jun, after which they became searchable and appeared as suggestions.

YouTube Kids filtering (Team YouTube FAQ, 1 Apr 2026) works in layers: automated filters read thumbnails, titles and the video itself, human reviewers spot check and refine the filters, and parent flags are reviewed around the clock and removed for everyone if upheld.

YouTube Kids excludes paid product placements, videos that push purchases, packaging and unboxing focused videos and excessive accumulation or consumption of products, so our songs should never feature branded toys or buying.
YouTube renamed the Partner Program's 'repetitious content' rule to 'mass produced content' on 15 Jul 2025; with 14 songs a week we must keep each song clearly different in story, setting and moves.
Community Guidelines strikes: a first violation is usually a warning that expires after 90 days with policy training; three strikes within 90 days can terminate the channel.
YouTube Kids added over 100 Sesame Street episodes in Jan 2026, so trusted educational brands are now direct competitors on the YouTube Kids learning shelf.
94% of teachers worldwide use YouTube in class (YouTube, Jan 2026), so classroom friendly songs (brain breaks, routines, counting) can earn repeat plays on school screens.

YouTube Music started labelling songs 'created primarily using generative AI' on 14 Oct 2026 (composition and vocals both AI) using partner data and its own detection, with the main YouTube app to follow; per YouTube's May 2026 policy a label alone does not change recommendations or monetisation.

Unlike YouTube, Spotify keeps AI badged artist profiles out of recommendations by default and Deezer removes AI detected tracks from algorithmic and editorial playlists, so AI made songs earn mostly on YouTube, not audio stores.
Suno songs are commercially usable (YouTube monetisation, distribution) only if made while on a paid Pro or Premier plan; free tier songs never convert, and the status stays after cancelling.

After the Nov 2025 Warner Music deal, Suno is moving to licensed models and capping downloads (about 20 a month on Pro, 60 on Premier), so we should download and back up every final song and stem as we make it.
The EU AI Act's transparency duties (Article 50) applied from 2 Aug 2026, with fines up to 15M EUR or 3% of turnover, adding another reason to disclose AI music clearly in descriptions.

YouTube confirmed (10 Aug 2026) that from 1 Feb 2027 new Partner Program applicants need 1,000 subscribers plus 8,000 public watch hours in 365 days, or 20M Shorts views in 90 days (double today); members admitted before then are grandfathered, so qualifying before February matters.

From 1 Feb 2027 Shorts pool revenue becomes a rolling test: a channel needs 10M qualified Shorts views in each rolling 90 days or its Shorts pool pay pauses that month; long form ads are unaffected, and partners must accept new modules by 31 Jan 2027.
A channel must also stay active to keep YPP from 2027: 1,000 watch hours in 365 days, 1M Shorts views in 90 days, or at least two long videos or five Shorts every 90 days.

The UK announced (15 Jun 2026) an under 16 social media ban modelled on Australia's (live since 10 Dec 2025), naming YouTube among covered platforms but leaving YouTube Kids outside it; rules are due by end 2026 and should apply from spring 2027.

YouTube Kids is a filtered copy of YouTube: automated filters check each video's thumbnail, title and content and any one can block it, with humans only spot checking; videos built around product packaging, urging kids to buy, paid placements or excessive consumption are kept out, so Bro Bros songs should never show branded toys or 'get yours' moments.

Since May 2026 YouTube shows a prominent AI label (under the player, or over a Short) only for photorealistic AI; for animated or stylised content like ours the disclosure appears only in the expanded description, and YouTube says a disclosure label does not change recommendations or monetisation, so ticking the AI box costs us nothing.

In AIR's 300 channel study (May 2025 to May 2026) kids and teens content was monetised on only about 32% of playbacks, the lowest of 13 niches, because made for kids videos cannot carry personalised ads, but it gets about a 22% lift in Q4; volume and reach, not rate per view, drive kids channel income.

On 15 Oct 2026 YouTube announced an invite only Monthly Shorts Bonus pilot for Partner Program creators in the US, UK, Germany, Brazil, Japan and South Korea; India is not in the first wave, another reason to build US and UK viewers.
From 26 Oct 2026 YouTube tests a 20 USD payout threshold (down from 100) for a random group of creators in the US, India and Indonesia, so small new channels may get first earnings sooner.

Since 29 Oct 2026 YouTube tests offering some channels with spam policy violations a 30 day cleanup lock (edit or delete videos, or wipe all videos but keep subscribers and handle) instead of termination; repetitive or templated uploads remain the main risk for high volume channels like ours.

Seasonal ad money: YouTube RPM runs about 0.5 times its spring baseline in January and about 1.8 to 2.5 times in December, and the two weeks before 25 Dec have the most competitive ad auctions, so our best holiday compilations should be live by the first days of December.

Precisify (Feb 2026): 80% of parents say their child asked for something seen in a YouTube ad while co viewing and 50% bought because of YouTube ads, which is why advertisers pay for kids views; our own videos must still never urge purchases, or they drop out of YouTube Kids.

Under COPPA and GDPR K, kids content must never ask children to send names, photos, videos or contest entries, nor use sign up links or tracking pixels, and that applies off YouTube too, so our Instagram captions should address parents and never invite kids to submit anything.

Since Aug 2025 YouTube's AI age estimation can treat signed in viewers it infers are minors as minors even on videos not marked made for kids, changing what is recommended and how ads run; COPPA 2.0 (protections to age 16) is still only proposed in the US.

In January 2026 YouTube terminated 16 mass produced AI channels with 35M subscribers and 4.7B lifetime views under its inauthentic content policy; enforcement judges a pattern across a channel's recent uploads (about the last 30), so one batch of templated songs can cut monetisation on every video.

After that purge faceless channels that never used AI also report demonetisation, while niche educational channels held up better; YouTube says AI labelled videos are not penalised and only mass produced, templated content without human creative input is targeted, so visible human craft (our own lyrics, stories, edits) is the protection.

A Kapwing test found about 21% of the first 500 videos recommended to a new account were AI slop, a New York Times check found over 40% of Shorts recommended after popular preschool videos were AI made, and 230 experts asked YouTube in April 2026 to ban AI content from YouTube Kids, so stricter AI rules for kids are likely.

India's DPDP rules define a child as anyone under 18, require verifiable parental consent before processing a child's data and ban tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted ads aimed at children, with fines up to 200 crore rupees; our Indian audience reach must stay on platform made for kids settings, never our own data collection.

YouTube's more prominent AI labels (May 2026) are not shown on YouTube Kids at all, which runs under separate policies, and animated AI videos on main YouTube only get a label tucked in the description; advocacy groups (Fairplay) now ask YouTube to stop recommending AI made for kids videos, so expect future limits aimed at animated AI kids content.

Neal Mohan's 2026 letter said YouTube would adapt its anti spam and anti clickbait systems to spot and demote low effort AI videos and strictly enforce synthetic media labels, so the defence for an AI assisted channel is clear human authorship and variety, not hiding AI use.

Since 10 Dec 2025 Australian under 16s are signed out of YouTube: they can still watch, but lose subscriptions, playlists, likes and wellbeing defaults, and parents lose supervised accounts; YouTube Kids is not affected, so in Australia (and later the UK and other copycat bans) the Kids app and signed out recommendations carry family viewing.

The EU's Digital Services Act guidelines on minors (Jul 2025) ask every platform kids may use to offer feeds children can reset and understand, private defaults, no overuse features like streaks or endless scroll, and clearly labelled child suitable ads; countdown timers and buy now prompts aimed at kids are discouraged, so our songs must never push kids to buy or demand things.

2026 estimates put Shorts RPM at about 0.10 to 0.32 USD per 1,000 views in the US and 0.09 to 0.19 in Australia, the UK, Germany and Canada, against 0.01 to 0.03 in India, Indonesia and the Philippines, so Shorts views from high income English markets earn about ten times more.

In Jul 2026 YouTube brought supervised kid accounts to the Middle East, North Africa and Turkiye, with three content levels, a Shorts timer that can switch Shorts off and, for every under 18, no personalised ads and autoplay off by default, so Arabic and Turkish families now get the same controls as the US and Europe.

The UK's first national screen guidance for under 5s (27 Mar 2026) says under 2s should use screens only for shared bonding activities, 2 to 5s at most an hour a day and none at meals or in the hour before bed, with slow paced content and no fast social media style videos; watching together is better than solo use.

Suno's 2026 rights terms (after its Nov 2025 Warner settlement): songs made on a free account can never be used commercially, and subscribing later gives no retroactive licence; songs made while subscribed carry commercial rights for streaming, downloads and sync with no revenue share, but users are no longer treated as owners of the songs.

Suno v6 (9 Sep 2026) runs on models co developed with Warner Music, BMG and Believe and all older models are being retired; free songs can no longer be downloaded and paid plans have monthly download limits (extra downloads cost more), so 14 songs a week plus remixes must fit our plan's download allowance.

A German court ruled in 2026, in a case brought by the collecting society GEMA, that Suno breached copyright, and Universal is not part of Suno's licensing deals, so prompts and lyrics must never name real artists or imitate known songs, keeping our catalogue clean if rules tighten.

Since mid 2025 Instagram treats adult managed accounts that mainly feature children with strict message settings, Hidden Words comment filtering, and no recommendations to or from potentially suspicious adults (also harder to find in Search); Meta has not said whether animated child characters count, so a small cut in odd adult reach is possible but parents still see us.

Instagram teen accounts default to a 13+ content level modelled on film ratings (US, UK, Australia and Canada since Oct 2025, India since 9 Apr 2026), with an even stricter Limited Content option; accounts flagged for age inappropriate posts lose teen followers and reach, so clean, gentle songs keep our Reels open to older siblings.

Because children under 13 cannot hold Instagram accounts, our Instagram audience is parents, carers and teens; captions and Reels should be written to parents (what the song helps with, a question for them) rather than to the child.

vidIQ models only about 10K USD of ad income for Tunes Kids' roughly 30M monthly Arabic views, a sign that Arabic made for kids views earn far less per view than English ones, so Arabic tracks are mainly for reach and brand growth.

YouTube Help lists what made for kids videos lose on their watch pages: autoplay on Home, cards and end screens, the video watermark (subscribe button), memberships, comments, donate and Super Chat, live chat, merch and tickets, notifications, personalised ads, Miniplayer playback, and save to playlist or Watch Later.

Made for kids channels also cannot use community posts, so channel news (new song days, holiday mixes) can only reach parents through Instagram, video titles and the channel banner, not YouTube posts.

Ads shown in YouTube Kids need pre approval from YouTube's policy team and food and drink, beauty and fitness, dating and political ads are barred, so YouTube Kids views earn less per view than main YouTube and should be judged by reach, not income.

Since 21 Oct 2026 YouTube automatically pauses features on channels that look hacked while it reviews them, usually within 24 hours and without touching monetisation, and since 29 Oct some channels facing spam termination get a 30 day lock to fix videos or appeal instead of instant removal.

Vietnam's National Assembly debated in 2026 restricting minors' use of some social apps and stricter identity checks for under 16s, citing Australia's ban (Dec 2025) and similar steps in Indonesia and France since Mar 2026; nothing is law yet, but signed out family viewing on TV and YouTube Kids is where Southeast Asian kids markets are heading.
Shorts that use licensed music from YouTube's library are capped at 60 seconds, but our own original Suno songs are not, though 25 to 40 seconds remains the performance sweet spot.

More than 200 child advocacy groups and child development experts (2026) asked YouTube to ban AI generated videos from the YouTube Kids app and give parents tools to limit AI content on main YouTube; for an AI assisted channel like ours, proof of human craft (original songs, designed characters, real story and learning goals) is the best protection if rules tighten.

YouTube's synthetic content disclosure rule exempts clearly unrealistic animation, so our 3D cartoons do not need an 'altered or synthetic' label, while anything that looks realistic (photoreal people, fake real world footage) would; scripts and captions written with AI also need no disclosure.

A Los Angeles jury found Google and Meta negligent in designing YouTube and Instagram and failing to warn users (25 Mar 2026, 6M USD, appeal planned), a bellwether for thousands of child harm cases with more trials due in 2026, so expect further kid safeguards such as less autoplay and scrolling that reduce passive binge views.

With pressure on attention grabbing design for kids, songs that end calmly, invite a real world action (go brush your teeth, time for bed) and avoid endless cliffhangers fit where regulators and parents are pushing YouTube, and are less likely to be hit by future limits.

The same guide says kids content runs at roughly half the normal CPM (made for kids ads are not personalised) and that Q4 and Ramadan bring 30 to 50% RPM spikes in the Middle East, so Arabic songs should be ready before Ramadan 2027 (about mid February).

AIR's 274 channel RPM study (Sep 2026) found Kids and Teens Shorts had a 45.7% monetised playback rate against only 12.1% for long form because of made for kids ad limits, about 2,156 Shorts views equal 1,000 long views for large kids channels, and Shorts made 41% of revenue for big kids channels posting 21+ Shorts a month.

In the same study a kids channel's long form RPM fell about 26% in months when it posted Shorts, and Shorts RPM by viewer country was 0.33 USD in the US against about 0.16 to 0.19 in Australia, the UK, Canada and Germany (correlational, vendor data).

Since March 2026 YouTube has been testing a mobile pop up that asks viewers to rate on a five point scale whether a video feels like AI slop, and it now labels AI made videos automatically from C2PA metadata and SynthID watermarks rather than relying only on creator disclosure, so visible human craft (story, gags, varied scenes) protects AI assisted songs like ours.

A 7.55M subscriber kids channel cut long uploads from 21 to 11 and raised Shorts from 10 to 23 in Q4 2025 against Q3, moved to 4K with TV safe text, higher contrast colours and audio mixed for TV speakers, and revenue grew about 34% on roughly 6% more views.

FluxNote's unsourced 2026 seasonal model puts November RPM around 3 times January and December about 3.6 to 5 times January, with the two weeks before 25 December the most competitive ad auctions of the year, so our best Christmas songs should be live by late November.

The New York Times' Feb 2026 test found the AI slop served to toddlers had warped faces, garbled text, no repetition, no story and no clip longer than 30 seconds; YouTube removed five cited channels from the Partner Program and YouTube Kids, so Bro Bros Shorts should always show a repeated hook and a tiny beginning, middle and end.

YouTube divides Shorts pool money with music rights holders by the number of licensed tracks used (one track takes roughly half of that Short's share), so Bro Bros Shorts built only on our own original songs keep the full creator share, a quiet money advantage over channels using library music.

Since March 2026 videos that show young subjects in distress with shocking imagery lose ad eligibility, so no crying or scared baby faces in Bro Bros thumbnails or opening frames, even for 'feelings' songs; show the happy ending face instead.

YouTube Premium Lite (no ads on most videos) is expanding to all Premium countries but keeps ads on music content and excludes YouTube Music, so song videos still earn ad money from Lite subscribers where other videos do not.
Content ID also scans multi language audio tracks, and YouTube skips auto dubbing on any video with a copyright claim, one more reason every Bro Bros track and dub uses only our own Suno music.

Sydney the Song Cat, a hand drawn kids song channel made over four years, was demonetised as 'inauthentic content' in spring 2026 even with a clean record, because it reused rigs and backgrounds; appeals with storyboards and voice recordings got template replies and it had to wait for a July re apply window.

In February 2026, shortly after YouTube removed big AI slop channels, popular kaiju and dinosaur animation channels also lost monetisation with no clear guidance, so reused 3D assets plus repetitive templates can be read as mass produced even when the work is original.

To protect monetisation every Bro Bros song should leave a visible human trail: an original story idea per video, varied scenes and choreography, real lyric changes rather than template swaps, and saved making of material (Suno prompts, Meshy prompts, Blender files, storyboards) to attach to any appeal.

The FTC's amended COPPA Rule (in force June 2025) had a compliance date of 22 April 2026, and YouTube used that date to require every creator, even non kids ones, to set the audience per channel or per video; FTC civil penalties reach about 53K USD per violation.

Once YouTube's systems apply a made for kids label the creator cannot change it, only appeal in Studio, and made for kids channels are excluded from the YouTube Shopping affiliate programme, so merchandise links must live off YouTube (website, Instagram).

Meta announced in June 2026 that its 13+ content setting for teen accounts (no suggestive, graphic, strong language, risky stunt or alcohol content in Explore, Reels and search) goes global across Instagram, Facebook and Messenger after India got it in April; clean family songs are not affected, but risky stunt jokes would be.
The Elf on the Shelf is a trademarked character and brand, so Bro Bros must design its own helper elf (different name, look and story) and never use that name or look in titles, tags or thumbnails.

Much Brazilian funk and phonk carries explicit lyrics and adult dance styles, so Bro Bros borrows only the rhythm (a bouncy tamborzao style drum pattern) in its own Suno songs, never the trending tracks or their moves.

CIMM notes that kids content earns lower CPMs, that ad tech often cannot work in COPPA compliant settings so children's videos are left out of programmatic buying, and that advertisers rarely buy YouTube made for kids inventory, which is why kids channel RPMs stay low and scale matters.

Since May 2026 YouTube auto detects and labels undisclosed photorealistic AI video, placing the label under the player on long videos and as an overlay on Shorts, but animated or stylised content (including animated AI music videos) only carries a disclosure in the expanded description.

YouTube says an AI disclosure label does not change recommendations or monetisation eligibility, and creators can correct a wrong label in Studio except for permanent labels on videos made with YouTube's own AI tools or carrying C2PA fully AI metadata.

Brazil's ECA Digital (child and teen online safety statute) has been fully in force since 17 Mar 2026 for services likely to be used by minors, including streaming and social platforms and foreign providers: it bans ad profiling of minors and compulsive design features and requires protective defaults and guardian linked accounts under 16.

Brazil's regulator scheduled administrative sanctions under ECA Digital from November 2026 and formal enforcement from January 2027, with fines up to 10% of Brazilian revenue; its decree on child influencers needs court approval to monetise real children, which does not touch an animated channel like ours.

Because laws in Brazil, the EU and the UK now target designs that encourage compulsive use, Bro Bros should avoid manipulative hooks aimed at kids (fake countdowns to keep watching, 'don't stop now' prompts) and keep endings that invite a calm goodbye.

leaves.t: Holiday nostalgia dances go viral each December: last year's awkward Charlie Brown-style party dance mashup united families (the characters are protected, but the goofy group-dance idea is not).
Winter-themed simple moves (snowflake arms, spins) became a global challenge in January 2026; easy, repeatable seasonal moves spread fastest.
Easy, low-impact, non-contact moves (whip, sway, wave, clap patterns) are the ones schools and families copy; simplicity is what makes a dance challenge spread.
Food and big machinery topics keep topping YouTube Shorts charts in November 2026; timely, event-like releases beat random uploads.

Late October trackers marked then and now nostalgia POVs and the wizard cat typing meme as fading and the costume loading reveal as already past its Halloween peak, confirming that Reels and TikTok formats now turn over in two to three weeks.

Toy industry talk at Toy Fair 2026 picked the shaggy, caramel coloured highland cow as the next trendy plush animal for kids, with capybaras (popular for over a year) and axolotls now at their peak; earlier cycles were llamas and owls, then hedgehogs and foxes.

Capybaras became the holiday 'it' animal of late 2024 on toy shelves and social media and stayed popular into 2026 because of their calm, friendly image, which makes a relaxed capybara friend a good calm down or bedtime character for us.

playbook: Major key, 4/4, 110-125 BPM for dance songs; keep one slow 60-70 BPM wind-down song in the week with no drum groove, a narrow melody and soft repeated phrases (the lullaby shape that calms babies in every culture).

One 1-2 bar hook repeated in every chorus, simple melody inside about 5 notes sitting mostly between middle C and A (C, F or G major), where preschoolers sing best; add nonsense syllables (la la, doo doo) kids can sing before they can talk.

Every lyric line has an action kids can copy (Total Physical Response): clap, jump, wiggle, freeze, stomp, with big quiet and loud contrasts (tiptoe, then jump, then a sudden stop) because toddlers move to changes in energy, not to the beat.
Use call-and-response or riddle lines ('What colour? RED!') with a short pause so kids can answer at home.

A tiny story that is easy to follow (one problem, one fix, one clear lesson such as kindness or a healthy habit) with one tempo change kids can act out, ending in a happy payoff; show people and places from many cultures.

A bright, young sounding lead voice (in Suno ask for 'bright youthful vocals' rather than 'children's choir', which often comes out uncanny); characters look into the camera and talk to the viewer, with spoken lines in their own [Spoken] section; master every song to about -14 LUFS with -1 dBTP peaks.

Subjects: family, animals, dogs, dinosaurs, vehicles, helpers, pretend play jobs and daily routines; each week make 2 songs as fresh Bro Bros twists on public domain rhymes (Wheels on the Bus, Old MacDonald, Five Little Ducks) with an animal or job twist and a learning tag in the title.

Half step key lift for the final chorus; start each song with a 2 bar clap or drum pattern (rhythm hooks babies first) and colour the arrangement with bright high register sounds (bells, xylophone, ukulele); reach the chorus by about 0:15, because our long songs hold viewers only about 20 seconds on average.

Camera and motion: calm cuts every 3 to 6 s, lead Bro centred and big, gentle constant background motion (drifting clouds, bubbles, stars) that matches the song, bright rounded visuals, big friendly eyes; no flashing, no sudden loud sounds.

Hide one learning point (counting, colours, routine, feelings, safety) and name it in the description; every week make at least one healthy habit song led by a friendly helper mascot (brush teeth for two minutes, wash hands) and one sharing or taking turns song, the topics behind this autumn's biggest kids breakouts.

Shorts and Reels: our skip rate in the first 3 s is 58 to 90%, so open on full body dancing at the chorus peak, a direct action call or a tiny mystery question ('Who took the cookie?'), with motion or text in the first half second; make each Short a new cut with its own hook that loops back to the start; keep music Shorts about 30 to 40 s and set each Short's related video link to its full song.

Thumbnails: one or two happy faces cropped big (both Bros, or a Bro with an animal friend; several face layouts beat single faces) (about 40% of the frame height), one clear action, one recognisable object, high contrast with a warm accent on a plain bright background (red and white or blue and orange), max 3 outlined words kept out of the bottom right corner; never scared, crying or shocked faces; test changes by hand because Test and Compare is off for kids videos.

Weekly long form: one 25 to 45 minute themed compilation (one topic, best performer first, a bonus blooper dance at the end) every Friday, because videos over 40 minutes break out far more often and kids compilations lift RPM; add a timestamp chapter per song named in the plain words parents search ('Brush Teeth Song', 'Dinosaur Stomp'); make the 25 Dec and 1 Jan Fridays holiday mega mixes; keep a 24/7 live stream of all songs running once we pass about 50 songs.

Languages: add re-sung audio tracks (not low quality AI voice swaps) to the best songs in Spanish, Portuguese, Indonesian and Arabic first, then Hindi; translate titles and descriptions of the top songs into 20 languages to test demand; keep one channel with multi audio rather than new language channels; make one bilingual English Spanish song a week (switch language each chorus), the lane where 123 Andres nearly doubled its views this autumn.

Originality and compliance: write our own lyrics, vary story situations and endings week to week (no template clones), tick the AI music disclosure on every upload, set made for kids per video, and make every Suno song on the paid plan.

Mix in older kid energy: at least two songs a week should be full body dance alongs (Danny Go! style) or movement games (freeze dance, going on a hunt, floor is lava, the top five hits of The Kiboomers) with a funny chantable nonsense word kids can shout, and make a part 2 of any game that wins; on Instagram post fewer, better Reels (the best 1 or 2 songs a day), captions as one keyword sentence plus a question to parents and at most 2 hashtags; group Shorts of one song family into a YouTube Shorts series and test two hooks per song with Trial Reels after 1,000 followers.
Every week, build 2 to 3 Shorts/Reels on a current trend format from the trend bank, adapted kid-safe with our own original song (never copyrighted trending audio).
Give each new song one signature 'challenge move' (sway, wave, clap, spin) simple enough for kids to copy, and teach it in a slow-motion Short.

Run 211 (TRENDS (late October rising formats for families: bow on the drop, rock paper scissors, pick your favourite; Thanksgiving gratitude cloth)): Virlo's tracker (29 Oct) shows family friendly formats rising: rock paper scissors over one plate of food, 'pick your favourite on three' and posing then bowing deeply on the beat drop; two joined the trend bank as Bro Bros games (two older ones left). Thanksgiving (26 Nov) brings back the gratitude tablecloth where kids trace their hands and families write thanks. Total 927.

Run 212 (global markets (US kids viewing split from CIMM, read along captions lift in Kenya)): CIMM (Jul 2026): US young children's video time is now 35% streaming, 32% YouTube and 16% short form, with linear TV down to about 6%, and children make up nearly a quarter of all YouTube viewing. In Kenya, adding read along captions to existing cartoons lifted child viewing 15% and adult co viewing 39%, a cheap idea for lyric captions in our songs. Total 932.

Run 213 (competitor deep dive (Rhymington Square monster songs, TinkaBop baby sensory)): Rhymington Square (Canada, 311K subs) has 291M views from only 74 songs, about 3.9M per video, with original monster songs and numbered sequels ('There's A Monster In My Tummy #2'), seasonal songs as its biggest cluster and about a quarter trend based. TinkaBop, a new baby sensory channel, shows the slow start: 11 videos, 5K subs, a bath time song its best at 18K views. Total 937.

Run 214 (TRENDS (trending kid animals: highland cow rising, capybara and axolotl peaking)): Toy Fair 2026 chatter names the shaggy highland cow as the next 'it' plush animal while capybaras and axolotls peak, following llamas and owls before them; capybaras were the holiday 'it' animal of late 2024. Our dancing animal friends format now uses these animals in original designs. Total 940.

Brazil's ECA Digital child online safety law is fully in force since March 2026 (sanctions from Nov 2026, enforcement Jan 2027): no ad profiling of minors, no compulsive design, guardian linked accounts under 16. Total 945.

Run 216 (algorithm experiments and data (our results already recorded today; Little Dot's video length whitepaper)): Metricool results were already recorded today, and AIR's kids cases were all in the tree, so this round read Little Dot Studios' Feb 2026 whitepaper (800+ channels, 11.2B monthly views): in 2024 a 2 hour video earned about 100 times a 20 minute one, but after YouTube's January 2025 update ultra long viewing fell over 90% within three months and recommended video length halved from 80 to 40 minutes, so mid length compilations (20 to 60 minutes) are the safe bet, not 3 hour uploads.
